title: Disk Controller and HBA Health
exclusions: Reports a qualified storage controller or Fibre Channel HBA/port whose normalized vendor/kernel state is warning, critical, degraded, failed, offline, blocked, linkdown, or whose controller reports degraded virtual drives. It does not assume every vendor's healthy word is `Optimal`, treat command failure or `unknown` as healthy, combine RAID-controller and FC-port semantics without component type, diagnose disk/array/fabric/path/driver/firmware cause, prove I/O or workload impact, or replace multipath, array, switch, filesystem, RAID-volume, or source-health monitoring. Missing expected components and invalid polls are coverage findings. The 15-minute poll, 45-minute window, severity, retention, and exceptions are local policy. No controller, path, port, array, or workload action is taken.
evidence: After deployment, retain host/controller/HBA/port/WWPN/slot/array/path/workload inventory; qualified vendor CLI/kernel/driver/firmware versions; least-privilege collector/parser/input revisions; representative raw StorCLI/SSA/FC sysfs output; documented normalization map by platform; expected-component, command, field, stale, duplicate, and identity health; version-controlled `storage_adapter_degraded` search, ACL, schedule, dispatches, and rows; vendor UI/array/fabric/multipath/workload corroboration and disposition; and dated controller-warning/critical, degraded-VD, FC-offline/blocked/linkdown, OK/online, unknown, missing, duplicate, replacement, recovery, and routing tests. This documentation-only review ran no vendor CLI and validated no production storage path.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a fixed completed 45-minute window, ingest the newest `component_type=raid_controller` sample for `host=server01`, `component_id=controller0`, `health=warning`, `operational_state=degraded`, and `degraded_virtual_drives=1`; expect one high row. Repeat an `fc_port` with `health=critical,operational_state=linkdown` and expect critical. Assert component/slot/WWPN, vendor source, state, degraded count, driver/firmware, event/index times, and `use_case=UC-1.4.10`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for qualified newest `health=ok,operational_state=online,degraded_virtual_drives=0`; for an old bad sample followed by newer healthy state; wrong source/type; blank identity/type; negative/nonnumeric count; unsupported state; duplicate; or out-of-window record. Separately prove command failure, `unknown`, missing expected controller/HBA/port, stale/no poll, parser drift, and component replacement create source-health findings and are never silently healthy.

dataSources: A host-local read-only collector emits `index=hardware sourcetype=hardware:storage_adapter` from qualified sources: Broadcom StorCLI `/call show all J` or supported JSON syntax for MegaRAID controllers/virtual drives; HPE Smart Storage Administrator CLI status output for supported Smart Array controllers; and Linux SCSI FC transport attributes under `/sys/class/fc_host/hostN` for FC HBA ports. Each event carries `host`, `component_type` (`raid_controller` or `fc_port`), stable `component_id`, slot/PCI identity, WWPN where relevant, canonical `health` and `operational_state`, numeric `degraded_virtual_drives`, vendor raw state, driver/firmware, command status, `_time`, and `_indextime`.
app: A deployment-owned Splunk app containing vendor-specific read-only collectors and parsers, a versioned normalization map, scripted inputs, expected-component/source-health searches, saved search, fixtures, exact maintenance lookup, dashboard, and runbook. Universal Forwarder can execute a collector but is not Splunkbase app 617; no single generic add-on normalizes RAID controllers and FC ports.
spl:
index=hardware sourcetype=hardware:storage_adapter earliest=-60m@m latest=-15m@m
| eval endpoint=lower(trim(host)), adapter_type=lower(trim(component_type)), adapter=lower(trim(component_id)), normalized_health=lower(trim(health)), normalized_state=lower(trim(operational_state)), degraded_vds=tonumber(degraded_virtual_drives)
| where len(endpoint)>0 AND adapter_type IN ("raid_controller","fc_port") AND len(adapter)>0 AND (isnull(degraded_vds) OR degraded_vds>=0)
| sort 0 endpoint adapter_type adapter -_time -_indextime
| dedup endpoint adapter_type adapter
| eval condition=case(normalized_health="critical" OR normalized_state IN ("failed","offline","blocked","linkdown"),"critical_adapter_state",normalized_health="warning" OR normalized_state="degraded","degraded_adapter_state",adapter_type="raid_controller" AND degraded_vds>0,"degraded_virtual_drives",true(),"normal")
| where condition!="normal"
| eval severity=if(condition="critical_adapter_state","critical","high"), event_time=strftime(_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), indexed_time=strftime(_indextime,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), use_case="UC-1.4.10"
| table event_time indexed_time endpoint adapter_type adapter slot pci_address wwpn condition severity normalized_health normalized_state degraded_vds vendor_state driver firmware command_status source_tool use_case
| sort 0 -severity endpoint adapter_type adapter
description: Reports the newest qualified RAID-controller or Fibre Channel port sample when its canonical health/state is degraded or failed, or a RAID controller reports degraded virtual drives. Component type, physical/FC identity, vendor state, driver, and firmware remain visible so unlike adapter semantics are not flattened into a generic non-Optimal string.
value: A controller, HBA, or FC-port problem can remove redundancy, force path failover, degrade storage, or precede loss of access while applications remain online. A source-qualified component signal helps teams verify array, fabric, multipath, disk, and workload evidence and engage the right vendor without assuming the adapter is the root cause.
implementation: Inventory every expected controller and HBA port, qualify read-only vendor CLI or Linux FC transport fields and a versioned canonical state map, and collect every 15 minutes under bounded timeout. Monitor missing/unknown/stale command results separately, save the delayed latest-state search, validate each vendor state and recovery against its management UI/CLI plus array/fabric/multipath evidence, then route by component and workload owner.
visualization: Lead with expected-component coverage, command/parser health, stale polls, and unknown states. Show controller and FC-port panels separately with host, slot/PCI/WWPN, canonical and vendor states, degraded virtual-drive count, driver/firmware, sample age, multipath/array/fabric context, workload, maintenance, and owner. Never merge an FC link state and RAID virtual-drive state into one unlabeled health score.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned state is real under the qualified source map, but it can be expected or misattributed.

1. **Approved controller/HBA firmware or driver maintenance** — reset, flash, link bounce, rescan, or failover can create temporary degraded/offline state. Match exact component/change, owner, bounded interval, protected workloads, expected sequence, and recovery.

2. **FC fabric or target maintenance** — an HBA port/link can be offline because of switch, optic, cable, zoning, target, or intentional path work while redundant paths carry I/O. Correlate fabric, remote ports, multipath, array, and change; do not replace the HBA by assumption.

3. **RAID rebuild or deliberate degraded test** — a virtual drive can remain degraded during an approved rebuild or fault exercise. Preserve progress, disk identity, redundancy, workload impact, vendor procedure, and expiry; degraded is still genuine.

4. **Component replacement/identity drift** — controller index or `hostN` can change after reboot/replacement. Reconcile serial/PCI slot/WWPN and inventory; do not transfer history on ephemeral numbering alone.

5. **Vendor CLI/parser mismatch** — tool/firmware updates can change JSON keys or state text. Command success is not controller health. Compare raw output and vendor UI, requalify parser fixtures, and surface unknown state.

6. **Stale sample after collector failure** — display age and command/source health; do not repeatedly page or clear from an old state.

Suppress notification only by exact stable component and condition with owner, reason, change, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress command/parser/unknown, missing expected component, stale/no poll, identity drift, or source-health controls.

cost.search_load_notes: One low-rate sample per controller or FC port every 15 minutes and a bounded latest-state search; collection runtime depends on vendor CLI and adapter count.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and typed component contract

Assign Linux/platform, storage/RAID, SAN/fabric, array, workload, Splunk data/content, and incident owners. Inventory each controller and FC HBA/port with stable serial, PCI address/physical slot, vendor/model, firmware/driver/tool, controller index, FC WWPN/WWNN/speed/fabric/target paths, attached arrays/disks/virtual drives, multipath design, workloads, maintenance, and escalation. Collectors need read-only status access and sysfs reads; they do not need configuration, rescan/reset, rebuild, disk state, zoning, path disable, or firmware rights. This review ran no source and asserts no compatibility matrix.

Do not flatten unlike devices. A RAID controller exposes controller and virtual-drive health through vendor CLI; an FC HBA port exposes transport/link state through Linux FC transport and vendor tools. Normalize only explicitly qualified source values into `health=ok|warning|critical|unknown` and `operational_state=online|degraded|failed|offline|blocked|linkdown|unknown`, preserving raw state and component type. Unknown/command failure is source health, not adapter failure or OK.

## Step 1 — Collect vendor/kernel state safely

For supported Broadcom MegaRAID, run documented StorCLI `/call show all` with the tool's supported JSON output form (often trailing `J`; verify exact release), parse command status separately from controller/VD state, and emit one controller event plus separate virtual-drive context. For HPE Smart Array, use the installed supported `ssacli`/SSA CLI status commands and a version-specific parser; retain raw output because JSON parity is not assumed. For FC, read `/sys/class/fc_host/hostN` attributes including port name/WWPN, node name, port state, speed and supported classes where exposed; supplement with remote-port/multipath evidence, not `/proc/scsi` text.

Emit host, component type/stable ID, ephemeral tool index, slot/PCI/WWPN, canonical health/state, vendor raw state, degraded virtual-drive count for controllers, driver/firmware/tool/parser version, command status/duration, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Poll every 15 minutes under timeout/concurrency limits. Never let a CLI hang overlap indefinitely.

Maintain expected components independent of fault data. Health reports command nonzero/timeout/permission, unsupported tool/controller, parser/key drift, unknown/null state, negative/nonnumeric count, missing/unexpected/replaced component, index/hostN/BDF remap, stale/future time, duplicate route, and index delay. A missing HBA or controller may be severe, but it is not a returned healthy state.

## Step 2 — Save and understand the SPL

Save sidecar SPL as `storage_adapter_degraded`. Run every 45 minutes over `earliest=-60m@m latest=-15m@m`, a complete 45-minute slice delayed 15 minutes. Tune from measured vendor-command and indexing delay while aligning schedule/range. The search validates typed identity and count, keeps the newest sample per host/type/component, and recognizes only canonical states. Critical covers explicit critical/failed/offline/blocked/linkdown; warning/degraded and any positive degraded-VD count route high. Healthy and unknown are not results; unknown remains source health. These priorities are local operational policy, not vendor equivalence.

## Step 3 — Validate each source independently

Build fixtures from authentic-shaped output for every supported StorCLI/SSA CLI/kernel/driver version. Test command success with healthy/degraded controller, command failure, zero/one/multiple degraded VDs, FC Online/Offline/Blocked/Linkdown/Unknown, case/whitespace, null/negative counts, duplicate IDs/routes, controller replacement, hostN/BDF remap, out-of-order/late data, old bad followed by healthy, and dispatch boundaries. Assert component-type-specific fields and source health.

In a disposable storage lab, compare indexed state with the exact vendor CLI and management UI, Linux FC sysfs, multipath, fabric switch, target/array, and workload I/O evidence. Exercise only vendor-approved path failover, disk/rebuild, link, or controller tests under change control, redundancy, backups, workload protection, out-of-band access, stop criteria, and rollback. Never fault production solely to test. Keep draft until owners approve source maps, fixtures, inventory, health, timing, dashboard, routing, and response.

## Step 4 — Investigate before storage action

Alert text identifies component type and says `reported degraded/offline`, not `storage outage`. Include stable/ephemeral identity, raw/canonical state, degraded VD count, driver/firmware/tool, event/index age, command/source health, paths/arrays/workloads, change, and owner. Responders verify current raw source; reconcile physical/FC identity; inspect controller event logs, virtual/physical drives, cache/battery, enclosures, kernel/SCSI, FC remote ports, switch/optic/zoning, target/array and multipath; assess workload errors/latency and redundancy; then follow vendor procedures. Never reset a controller/HBA, fail/offline a disk/path, start/stop rebuild, rescan, change zoning, migrate/reboot, or update firmware automatically.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot and close

- **CLI command fails:** separate tool/install/permission/device/timeout/parser failure from hardware state; preserve stderr/status and keep coverage unhealthy.
- **Controller says healthy but VD degraded:** the degraded-VD count intentionally alerts; inspect exact virtual and physical drive topology.
- **FC port offline:** verify expected administrative/topology state, cable/optic/switch/zoning/target and redundant paths before assigning HBA cause.
- **Identity changes:** map serial/PCI slot/WWPN and lifecycle; do not key exceptions to controller index or `hostN` alone.
- **Vendor UI disagrees:** align target controller/port, clocks, polling time, firmware/tool/parser, and raw state; use raw vendor evidence until normalized parity is restored.
- **No workload impact:** redundancy may be carrying traffic. Preserve the degraded condition and quantify remaining paths/redundancy instead of closing as false.

Close after source health and current adapter state are verified, stable identity/topology is reconciled, array/fabric/multipath/workload impact and cause are documented, approved repair/change or accepted risk is complete, temporary exceptions expire, and an observation interval confirms expected state.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the cards and ports that connect a server to its storage. If their own tools report a degraded controller, disk group, or storage link, we show the exact component so the team can check the array and network before changing anything.
